articles.title: Red Roses suffer back-to-back defeats for first time in a decade as Canada make statement
articles.summary: WXV: Canada 31-22 England. England beaten in Ottawa for third loss in past 74 matches. History-makers, era-enders, giant-slayers. Last Friday’s breaking of England’s unbeaten run was a statement win for Canada but backing it up to deal the Red Roses their first consecutive loss in a decade, this…
body: On a cold Ottawa night, the Canadians played with freedom and pace to down England once again. The captain Sophie de Goede laid bare why she is the reigning world player of the year with a hat-trick and some excellent defensive work and Julie Omokhuale also stood out among a good team performance.

For England, well they were looking for a response to that record-ending defeat but it never came. A strong and confident start ebbed into a scrappy and hesitant overall outing which they will want to put right for their final WXV Global Series match against the USA next Friday. But there were some positives for the visitors, namely the skipper Meg Jones. The captain, who turned 30 on Friday, was imperious in defence and Maddie Feaunati had another good game in the hour she was given.

An Owellian atmosphere was created for those watching from home with the pitch having a grey tinge to it, a dystopian world isn’t usually compared to that of the vibrant and action-packed women’s rugby sphere but it may have felt like another world for England players losing back-to-back games. It was their third loss in 74 matches, so the panic won’t set in, but this result will unsettle them.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders unionize after years of fighting for fair pay
articles.summary: Team elects to voluntarily recognize union. Squad members have advocated for better wages. The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders have unionized, in a watershed labor victory that comes after years of fighting for fair pay.
body: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association (DCCA) was voluntarily recognized by the Cowboys as the collective bargaining representative for the cheerleading squad, according to a Friday news release. The recognition came after “meaningful discussion” between the Cowboys organization and the DCCA, and the parties are set to begin collective bargaining.

“The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are an esteemed part of the Cowboys organization, deeply respected for the talent and dedication they exhibit,” the DCCA said in a statement. “They remain one of the most sought-after opportunities for talented dancers worldwide.”

Established in 1961, one year after the football team played its inaugural season in the NFL, the Cowboys cheerleaders are among the most recognizable dance groups in the world. The squad’s national profile rose as they were chronicled in a Netflix series, America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, which released its third season in June.
For decades, the franchise has faced scrutiny over the cheerleaders’ low salaries, despite their enduring pop culture relevance.

articles.title: F1 crown in reach for Kimi Antonelli at bumpy Austin circuit drivers insist is ‘unacceptable’
articles.summary: Mercedes youngster could become youngest title winner. Max Verstappen says bumpy track makes drivers ‘suffer’ The Formula One world championship is within reach for Kimi Antonelli at the US Grand Prix in Austin this weekend.
body: The 20-year-old Antonelli will become Formula One’s youngest world champion if he claims the title at the Circuit of the Americas on Sunday, eclipsing Sebastian Vettel’s record from 2010, when the German driver was 23 and Antonelli was four. It is an outside chance, as the Italian has acknowledged. He must win while needing his rivals to endure a poor day. His Mercedes teammate George Russell would have to finish outside the top eight and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton outside the top four.

Nonetheless, while Antonelli knows the title race is in effect over, he is keeping the cool head that has brought him to this point with such alacrity. The Mercedes ship, helmed by his race engineer Pete Bonnington, who was alongside Hamilton for his six titles with the team, is steady as she goes.

“We had a meeting with Bono this morning and we said: ‘Just have fun,’” Antonelli said. “It’s the same mindset I’ve had all year. One race at a time. Just try to do the best I can every race weekend, and then we’ll see.”

articles.title: MotoGP Academy Badges Racing Schools to Chase New Talent
articles.summary: Photo by MotoGP. MotoGP is opening a new grassroots avenue for finding and developing new talent with the launch of the MotoGP Academy, a seal of approval the championship will award to racing schools and institutions worldwide that meet its standards on and off the track.
body: The goal is to create a network of racing schools around the world - and in particular regions that are currently underserved - to train young talent. To be clear, the MotoGP Academy program isn't going to be building and running new schools, but rather, MotoGP is licensing its brand and providing resources to existing schools that meet a standard criteria.

The Academy sits alongside the Moto4 series (previously known as the Talent Cups) and the JuniorGP paddock under the Road to MotoGP umbrella. The thinking echoes how the Asian and British Talent Cups were formed last decade to funnel regional talent toward the world championship.

To earn the seal of a proval, a school must satisfy criteria across four categories: infrastructure, training methodology, technical execution, and visibility of the brand. Qualified schools will continue to operate independently, but will have access to tailored toolkits, activation support, discounts on MotoGP products, and MotoGP Academy branding. MotoGP will benefit from having access to grassroots programs that can further grow its overall brand.

articles.title: Newey responds to Horner's 'abandon ship' criticism
articles.summary: Adrian Newey suspects Christian Horner did not "fully understand" his "pain and frustration" during Red Bull's fallow years with Renault engines after criticism of him in the former team principal's new book.
body: Horner as team principal and Newey as technical chief worked together with huge success across 19 years at Red Bull, enjoying two periods of sustained title-winning form with first Sebastian Vettel in 2010-2013 and then Max Verstappen in 2021-2024.
But between those periods Red Bull took a back seat to Mercedes' dominance of the sport following the arrival of turbo-hybrid engines in 2014.

Red Bull initially continued to be powered by Renault, as in their four title-winning years under the previous rules era, but the French manufacturer struggled with the new regulations, which compromised the performance of the team's Newey-designed car.

Writing in his newly-released autobiography, Drive, Horner recounted a period mid-way through 2014 when he became disappointed in Newey after the legendary designer had received an offer to join Ferrari and was mulling whether to leave.

articles.summary: Issa Diop escaped what Oliver Glasner called "a clear red card" during Ipswich's 1-1 draw with Nottingham Forest - but the incident split opinion, so was it the right call or not?

On co-commentary, Lee Hendrie reckoned Diop was "really lucky" and criticised the reasoning from the referee. Post-match, Ashley Young defended the decision.
